title: agentopt approved cases
description: Durable, human-approved regression cases — the committed file `agentopt.cases.yaml` at the project root (NOT under .agentopt/, which is disposable tool state). agentopt proposes cases into .agentopt/review/generated-cases.yaml; a human promotes approved ones here, where they are version-controlled, shared with CI, and survive workspace cleanup. Compiled ALONGSIDE GOALS.md. `group` is an organizational LABEL (free text, not a foreign key); `goal_id` is reserved (inert) for a future strict reference into named GOALS goals. Legacy prose examples in GOALS.md keep compiling too.

group.description: Optional organizational label for reporting, clustering, and coverage. NOT a foreign key — named 'group', not 'goal', so it is never mistaken for a strict reference and its meaning can't shift under a later migration.

goal_id.description: RESERVED for the constraint-tier work: a strict reference to a defined goal id. Accepted but NOT resolved or consumed by the compiler today — do not rely on it having any effect yet.

expected.description: The check to assert. MUST map onto agentopt's existing compiled check vocabulary — it is not a new check language. Kept as a closed set here so the compiler translates it to the same checks GOALS.md produces.

locked.description: When true: automated processes (optimizer, reflector, review) cannot delete, weaken, or rewrite this case. Only an explicit human-authorized command or a direct file edit can change it.

critical.description: A HARD CONSTRAINT: a fail-closed veto that runs BEFORE quality. A candidate that regresses this case (or stops executing it validly) is rejected outright — a gain elsewhere can never trade it away. Use for safety/business-critical behavior.

weight.description: Priority weight WITHIN the quality dimension (a soft lever, unlike the binary `critical` veto). Scales this case's effect size when the gate weighs a candidate's net quality gain, so a gain or regression on a high-priority case counts more. Never trades against reliability/cost/holdout. 1 = normal.

split.description: Train/holdout assignment. 'auto' uses the normal salt-based rotation. An explicit 'train'/'holdout' PINS the case deterministically, overriding rotation — a locked holdout case must also be withheld from candidate generation.

redaction.description: What was redacted from the trace before this case was written (shown to the human at approval time).

expectation.description: A closed set that maps 1:1 onto agentopt's EXISTING compiled check types (evals/models.py Check union) — NOT a new check language. Exactly one key. Extend only in lockstep with that union; a kind with no backing check must never be added. (No `output_matches`/regex here: the compiler has no regex check yet — that is a v2 item requiring a new RegexCheck in both packages.)

quality.description: -> JudgeCheck, SELF-CONTAINED: carries its own rubric (+ optional anchors), NOT a reference to a GOALS quality. Chosen because GOALS qualities have no stable identity yet (compiler-generated ids shift on insert/rename/collision); a cross-file quality reference is deferred to the goal_id work.

provenance.description: Where the expectation came from. The expected behavior is NEVER the raw production answer just because it occurred — it must trace to a human-confirmed source.

source.description: How the expectation was established. 'production_trace' still requires human approval to become active.

trace_id.description: Originating run id; kept local, never shipped externally.
